```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_seurat <- requireNamespace("Seurat", quietly = TRUE)
```

# Overview

picklerick reads single-cell files through the SCX engine, a Rust library
that streams a count matrix in chunks of cells and never holds a Python or
HDF5 object graph in R. One reader function, `read_h5ad()`, handles every
format: the format is detected from the file's content, not its extension.

| Format | Produced by | Read | Written |
|---|---|:-:|:-:|
| AnnData `.h5ad` | anndata, scanpy | yes | yes |
| AnnData Zarr store (`.zarr` directory, v2 or v3) | `adata.write_zarr()` | yes | yes (v3) |
| H5Seurat (`.h5seurat`, dgCMatrix or BPCells-backed) | SeuratDisk, Seurat v5 | yes | yes |
| 10x Genomics HDF5 (`.h5`) | Cell Ranger | yes | |
| 10x MatrixMarket directory (`matrix.mtx.gz` + features + barcodes) | Cell Ranger | yes | |
| BPCells matrix directory | BPCells | yes | X only |

Each file gives you the same choice of R object: a `SingleCellExperiment`,
a `Seurat` object, a light AnnData-like handle, or the raw pieces as a list.
Large matrices can stay on disk as a `DelayedMatrix`.

This vignette uses a 6-cell by 5-gene dataset shipped with the package in
every input format. Row 1 has no counts and one gene is expressed in a single
cell, so empty cells and sparse genes are part of every example.

```{r}
library(picklerick)

extdata <- system.file("extdata", package = "picklerick")
h5ad     <- file.path(extdata, "tiny.h5ad")
tenx_h5  <- file.path(extdata, "tiny_10x.h5")
mtx_dir  <- file.path(extdata, "tiny_mtx")
h5seurat <- file.path(extdata, "tiny_v4.h5seurat")
```

# Looking before reading

`inspect()` reads only metadata: shape, column names, embedding keys, and
per-layer sparsity from the row pointer. Nothing from the count matrix is
loaded, whatever the file size.

```{r}
info <- inspect(h5ad)
str(info[c("format", "n_obs", "n_vars", "obs_cols", "var_cols", "obsm_keys")])
info$layers
```

# Reading into a SingleCellExperiment

The default target is a `SingleCellExperiment`. Features are rows and cells
are columns, the Bioconductor convention. `obs` becomes `colData()`, `var`
becomes `rowData()`, `obsm` entries become `reducedDims()`, layers become
assays of their own name, and `obsp` graphs become `colPairs()`. The AnnData
`X` becomes the `counts` assay, unless a layer is already called `counts`,
as here (scanpy keeps raw counts there next to a normalised `X`); then `X`
keeps its name.

```{r}
sce <- read_h5ad(h5ad)
sce
SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "X")
SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)
```

Column encodings survive the trip: categoricals become factors, pandas
nullable integer and boolean columns keep their `NA`s.

```{r}
str(as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)))
```

## Unstructured metadata (`uns`)

`uns` can be large and deeply nested, so it is not parsed by default. The
`uns()` accessor reads one key at a time from the file when you need it, or
`parse_uns = TRUE` materialises all of it into `metadata()`.

```{r}
uns(sce)                 # the keys, without reading the values
uns(sce, "params")
```

# The same reader for every format

Content detection means the file name does not matter. The four files below
hold the same cells and genes.

```{r}
for (f in c(h5ad, tenx_h5, mtx_dir, h5seurat)) {
  x <- read_h5ad(f)
  cat(sprintf("%-20s %s  %d x %d\n", basename(f), inspect(f)$format, nrow(x), ncol(x)))
}
```

A 10x file carries only the matrix and its names, so its `colData()` is
empty. An H5Seurat file is read from its `RNA` assay: the `counts` layer
becomes the `counts` assay and its other layers come along as assays too.

```{r}
colnames(SummarizedExperiment::colData(read_h5ad(tenx_h5)))
read_h5ad(h5seurat)
```

## AnnData Zarr stores

A Zarr store is a directory. Reading one is the same call; `read_zarr()` is
an alias that makes the intent visible. Here we make one with `convert()`,
which streams one file into another format without building any R object.

```{r}
zarr <- file.path(tempdir(), "tiny.zarr")
convert(h5ad, zarr)
inspect(zarr)$format
identical(
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(read_zarr(zarr), "X"),
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "X")
)
```

# Reading into a Seurat object

`as = "Seurat"` builds a Seurat v5 object: `counts` from `X`, cell metadata
from `obs`, feature metadata on the assay, reductions from `obsm`. `obsp`
graphs are not attached and are dropped with a warning.

```{r, eval = has_seurat}
obj <- read_h5ad(h5ad, as = "Seurat")
obj
head(obj[[]])
```

`constructor = "fast"` assembles the `Assay5` directly from the matrix just
read rather than through `CreateSeuratObject()`, which copies it twice. It
is used only when the names and metadata need none of the sanitising
`CreateSeuratObject()` does, and falls back otherwise. On 10,000 cells it
removes the extra 500 MB and most of the construction time; on six cells it
makes no visible difference.

```{r, eval = has_seurat}
obj_fast <- read_h5ad(h5ad, as = "Seurat", constructor = "fast")
identical(SeuratObject::LayerData(obj_fast, "counts"), SeuratObject::LayerData(obj, "counts"))
```

# Deferring the R object

Building a `SingleCellExperiment` costs a few seconds of S4 warm-up however
small the data. `as = "AnnData"` returns a light handle instead: a shape, the
names, and components that are built on first use and cached. Convert it
later with `as_sce()` or `as_seurat()`.

```{r}
a <- read_h5ad(h5ad, as = "AnnData")
a
dim(a)
a$obs_names
a$X                                   # built now, cached
sce_from_handle <- as_sce(a)
```

`as = "list"` returns the raw pieces (index vectors, column lists, the CSR
triplet) for callers assembling something else.

```{r}
names(read_h5ad(h5ad, as = "list"))
```

# Leaving the matrix on disk

`lazy = TRUE` reads the metadata and wraps the matrix in a `DelayedMatrix`
instead of loading it. For an `.h5ad` the wrapper is
`HDF5Array::H5SparseMatrix` when that package is installed, the conventional
seed for that layout. For every other format, and for `.h5ad` without
HDF5Array, it is `PicklerickMatrix()`, a seed that reads blocks through SCX.

```{r}
lazy <- read_zarr(zarr, lazy = TRUE)
x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(lazy, "X")
class(x)
DelayedArray::seed(x)
```

Selecting cells reads only those cells from the store: the row pointer is
loaded, then just the selected rows' slices of the values and column indices.
Block operations walk the matrix `chunk_size` cells at a time.

```{r}
x[, c("cell2", "cell5")]
as.matrix(x[, c("cell2", "cell5")])
DelayedArray::colSums(x)
```

`PicklerickMatrix()` can also be built directly, and can expose a layer.

```{r}
m <- PicklerickMatrix(zarr, layer = "counts", chunk_size = 2L)
m
DelayedArray::chunkdim(DelayedArray::seed(m))
```

# Writing

`write_h5ad()` writes a `SingleCellExperiment` as `.h5ad`, and `convert()`
streams any readable file into `.h5ad`, `.h5seurat` or a Zarr v3 store,
chosen by the output extension. Both bound memory by the chunk size, not
the dataset.

```{r}
tenx <- read_h5ad(tenx_h5)
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "roundtrip.h5ad")
write_h5ad(tenx, out)
identical(
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(read_h5ad(out), "counts"),
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(tenx, "counts")
)
convert(h5ad, file.path(tempdir(), "tiny.h5seurat"))
inspect(file.path(tempdir(), "tiny.h5seurat"))$format
```

sessionInfo()
